title: Discrete logarithms in finite semigroups

problem.name: Discrete logarithms in finite semigroups
problem.statement_latex: Given $g,x$ in a uniquely encoded finite semigroup $S$, find $a\ge1$ with $g^a=x$, or decide that none exists. Powers have an eventual tail and cycle; the resource is oracle operations and gates.
problem.statement_text: Given $g,x$ in a uniquely encoded finite semigroup $S$, find $a\ge1$ with $g^a=x$, or decide that none exists. Powers have an eventual tail and cycle; the resource is oracle operations and gates.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.
strength.description_text: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.
evidence.description_text: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.

hardware.description_latex: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.
hardware.description_text: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(\log|S|)$ quantum time by Childs--Ivanyos, using period finding to recover the tail and cycle and then solving a cyclic-group logarithm.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(\log|S|)$ quantum time by Childs–Ivanyos, using period finding to recover the tail and cycle and then solving a cyclic-group logarithm.

classical.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(|S|^{1/2})$ generic semigroup operations by baby-step--giant-step methods for the tail/cycle and the resulting group discrete logarithm. Structured platforms inherit their faster group-logarithm algorithms.
classical.headline_text: $\widetilde O(|S|^{1/2})$ generic semigroup operations by baby-step–giant-step methods for the tail/cycle and the resulting group discrete logarithm. Structured platforms inherit their faster group-logarithm algorithms.
